title: Understand Functions Review Test
description: Identify inputs, reason about unique outputs, and explain representations and counterexamples.

questions.questionText: A machine assigns input 21 to output 25. Under the same rule, can that same input also have output 26?
questions.correctAnswer: No; one input cannot have two different outputs.
questions.explanation: A function assigns exactly one output to each input in its domain. Changing the output for the same input would violate that rule.
options: Yes; functions allow any number of outputs per input.
Yes; both outputs are positive.
No; one input cannot have two different outputs.
No; outputs must equal inputs.

questions.questionText: The complete relation is (21, 7), (22, 7), (23, 7). Is it a function of the first coordinate?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; each input has one output.
questions.explanation: Different inputs may share an output. Check each first coordinate separately; none has conflicting outputs.
options: No; the output 7 repeats.
No; a function must increase.
Yes; any three pairs form a function.
Yes; each input has one output.

questions.questionText: The function rule is: add 5 to the input. What is the output for input 21?
questions.explanation: Apply the rule to the input: 21 + 5 = 26. The result is the output.

questions.questionText: A rule sends 21 to 30. Which number is the input?
questions.explanation: In an input-to-output statement, the starting number is the input. The number it is sent to is the output.

questions.questionText: The complete list is (21, 3), (21, 8). Which fact prevents it from being a function of x?
questions.explanation: The conflict is two different outputs for one input. Different outputs at different inputs would be allowed.
options: There are only two pairs.
The outputs are different numbers.
Input 21 has outputs 3 and 8.
The numbers are all positive.

options: No; the output 7 repeats.

questions.questionText: The function rule is: add 5 to the input. What is the output for input 22?

questions.questionText: A function already contains (21, 4) and (22, 6). Which new pair would create a conflict?
questions.explanation: The existing input 21 already has output 4. Assigning it 9 would give two outputs; the other options introduce new inputs.

questions.questionText: A relation records (21, 5), (21, 5), (22, 8). Does the repeated identical record break the function rule?
questions.correctAnswer: No; the repeated input still has only one distinct output.
questions.explanation: Recording the same pair twice adds no new assignment. A repeated input breaks the rule only when its outputs disagree.
options: Yes; an input may never be recorded twice.
No; the repeated input still has only one distinct output.
Yes; outputs must be unique.
No; duplicate inputs can have any outputs.

questions.questionText: A function doubles its input, then subtracts 3. Which input produces output 43?
questions.explanation: Work backward: add 3 to 43, then divide by 2. Check: 2(23) - 3 = 43.

questions.questionText: At a school with 31 students, each student is assigned exactly one homeroom. Several students share a room. Is student-to-homeroom a function?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; each student has exactly one assigned room.
questions.explanation: Inputs and outputs need not be numbers. Shared outputs are allowed; the unique room assigned to each student is what matters.
options: No; a room cannot be shared.
No; the inputs are not numbers.
Yes; each student has exactly one assigned room.
Yes; every relation involving students is a function.

questions.questionText: Only inputs 21 and 22 are allowed. Both are assigned output 0. How many distinct output values does this function have?
questions.explanation: There are two inputs but only one distinct output value, zero. A constant function is still a function.
options: It is not a function.
